changes: Durable modal reservations retain their captured invoker. After it is removed, the next launch recovers the slot unless an actual modal remains open.
The generated destructive renderer checks its reservation owner again after derived-value preparation; an abandoned or superseded attempt opens no dialog and dispatches nothing.
The existing held-preparation integration regression now exercises both retained and abandoned ownership without adding a new analyzer-inventory declaration.

The isolated Test specimen host can reject BatchIncrement Amount=3 with a support-safe field map. The opt-in is disabled outside Test or without specimen configuration; corrected values use the existing authorized service.

The mapped-rejection browser regression proves summary focus, native Chromium accessibility-tree error description, single inline error, no duplicate lifecycle announcement, keyboard Dismiss focus, retained values and errors, and confirmed corrected retry.
Owned-process readiness parses only complete listening lines and ignores malformed addresses; split IPv4 and IPv6 log chunks are covered.
validationNotes: The initial default SourceTools lane passed 1297/1297 and Shell passed 3089/3091. After the final runtime changes, the required builds, focused SourceTools 148/148, focused Shell 93/93, native browser regressions 3/3, TypeScript check, and owned-process regressions 4/4 passed.

The initial broad browser run was 44/48; its forced-colors failure used the default 5070 because the temporary configuration did not also supply BASE_URL to an explicitly created context. The recheck supplied that environment value.

The broad browser recheck was 43 passed, 5 failed, 1 skipped.
